chunks.text: For assessment year 2026-27 the new regime slabs are: nil up to Rs 4 lakh, 5% from Rs 4 lakh to Rs 8 lakh, 10% from Rs 8 lakh to Rs 12 lakh, 15% from Rs 12 lakh to Rs 16 lakh, 20% from Rs 16 lakh to Rs 20 lakh, 25% from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 24 lakh, and 30% above Rs 24 lakh, plus 4% health and education cess.

Salaried taxpayers get a standard deduction of Rs 75,000 under the new regime. A resident individual with taxable income up to Rs 12 lakh pays no tax because of the rebate of up to Rs 60,000, so a salary up to Rs 12.75 lakh can be tax free after the standard deduction.

For assessment year 2026-27 the old regime slabs for individuals under 60 are: nil up to Rs 2.5 lakh, 5% from Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 5 lakh, 20% from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh, and 30% above Rs 10 lakh, plus 4% cess. The old regime standard deduction for salaried taxpayers is Rs 50,000 and the rebate is up to Rs 12,500 for taxable income up to Rs 5 lakh.

Under the old regime, section 80C allows deductions up to Rs 1.5 lakh, an additional NPS contribution under section 80CCD(1B) up to Rs 50,000, and health insurance premiums under section 80D up to Rs 25,000 for self and family, rising to Rs 50,000 for senior citizens.

title: Income tax regimes AY 2026-27: slabs, rebate, and deductions
